extracted.intended_audience: bidder and target companies involved in tender offers; securities lawyers; corporate compliance officers; investment bankers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulation 14D/14E rules specifying scope, exemptions, conditions, and definitions applicable to tender offers (including special rules for foreign private issuers). Useful for preparing, evaluating, or advising on tender offers under U.S. securities law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Regulations 14D and 14E
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation 14D (§§ 240.14d-1 through 240.14d-101) applies to any tender offer subject to section 14(d)(1) of the Act; Regulation 14E (§§ 240.14e-1 through 14e-8) applies to any tender offer for securities (other than exempted securities) unless otherwise noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes offers for classes described in section 14(d)(1) and offers made by affiliates of the issuer. Establishes baseline applicability for all subsequent requirements and exemptions in the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate compliance for foreign private issuers (Canadian issuers) — paragraph (b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements of sections 14(d)(1)-(7), Regulation 14D/14E, Schedules TO and 14D-9, and Rule 14e-1 shall be deemed satisfied for tender offers for securities of an issuer incorporated/organized under Canadian law if: the issuer is a foreign private issuer, is not a registered investment company, less than 40% of the class outstanding is held by U.S. holders, and the tender offer is subject to and the bidder complies with applicable Canadian laws/regulations/policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two provisos: (1) For cash-only consideration in offers subject to 14(d)(1), entire disclosure document(s) must be filed with Commission on Schedule 14D-1F and disseminated to U.S. shareholders per Canadian law; (2) If consideration includes bidder securities, any registration statement/prospectus must be filed with the Commission along with Schedule 14D-1F and disseminated (with home jurisdiction documents) to U.S. shareholders per Canadian law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptions re foreign private issuer and U.S. ownership (Notes)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of tender offers eligible under Rule 14d-1(b), the issuer will be presumed a foreign private issuer and U.S. holders presumed to hold <40% of outstanding securities unless (a) U.S. trading volume exceeded Canadian trading over prior 12 months, (b) issuer filings indicate U.S. holders hold ≥40%, or (c) offeror has actual knowledge U.S. ownership ≥40%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presumption may be rebutted by trading volume comparisons, disclosure in issuer filings, or actual knowledge. Volume comparisons use published figures from exchanges and CDN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission adequacy determination for foreign regulatory regimes (Note 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if an exemption from Canadian regulatory provisions is granted, the tender offer may proceed under paragraph (b) only if the Commission by order determines the applicable Canadian provisions are adequate to protect investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission retains jurisdiction to assess whether home jurisdiction protections are adequate despite local exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier I exemption — overview
rubrics_metrics.description: A tender offer for securities of a foreign private issuer is exempt from sections 14(d)(1)-(7), Regulation 14D, Schedules TO and 14D-9, and §§ 240.14e-1 and 14e-2 if specified Tier I conditions are satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier I sets a safe-harbor/exemption subject to meeting multiple conditions enumerated in paragraph (c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier I condition — U.S. ownership limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in certain pendency scenarios, U.S. holders must not hold more than 10 percent of the class of securities sought in the offer (determined under Instructions 2 or 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 10% threshold is measured per the Instructions; exceptions apply if offer commenced during pendency of prior bidder in reliance on this paragraph or § 240.13e-4(h)(8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier I condition — Equal treatment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The bidder must permit U.S. holders to participate on terms at least as favorable as those offered to any other holder of the same class; several sub-exceptions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sub-exceptions include: (i) Registered exchange offers: bidder need not extend to holders in jurisdictions prohibiting offer/sale after good-faith registration efforts, but must offer same cash alternative to those holders; (ii) Exempt exchange offers: similar carve-out with same cash-alternative requirement; (iii) Cash-only consideration: bidder may offer U.S. holders only cash if it reasonably believes cash is substantially equivalent to non-U.S. consideration, and must provide either market trading data (if offered security is a 'margin security') or an independent expert opinion (if not a margin security) upon request; (iv) Disparate tax treatment: loan notes offered solely to provide tax advantages not available in U.S. need not be offered to U.S. holders if not listed/registered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier I condition — Informational documents dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: The bidder must disseminate any informational document to U.S. holders, including amendments, in English on a comparable basis to holders in the home jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If disseminated by publication in home jurisdiction, must publish in the U.S. in a manner reasonably calculated to inform U.S. holders. For offers described in section 14(d)(1), published informational documents must be furnished to the Commission on Form CB by the first business day after publication; foreign bidders must also file Form F-X simultaneously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier I condition — Investment company exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The issuer of the securities subject to the tender offer must not be an investment company registered or required to be registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940, other than a registered closed-end investment company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures Tier I exemption does not apply to most investment companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier II eligibility conditions (paragraph (d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A person conducting a tender offer meeting conditions in paragraph (d)(1) is entitled to specified exemptive relief in paragraph (d)(2): (i) subject company is a foreign private issuer and not an investment company (except registered closed-end), (ii) U.S. holders do not hold more than 40% of the class (with certain pendency exceptions), (iii) bidder complies with all applicable U.S. tender offer laws/regulations other than specifically exempted requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier II provides broader relief than Tier I but uses a higher U.S. ownership threshold (40%) and requires compliance with remaining U.S. tender offer rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier II exemptions — loan notes tax-advantage carve-out
rubrics_metrics.description: If bidder offers loan notes solely for tax advantages not available in the U.S. and the notes are neither listed nor registered, the loan notes need not be offered to U.S. holders notwithstanding § 240.14d-10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits tax-driven instruments to be excluded from U.S. participation under specified conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier II exemptions — separate U.S. and foreign offers
rubrics_metrics.description: A bidder meeting paragraph (d)(1) may separate the offer into multiple offers (one to U.S. holders and one or more to non-U.S. holders); the U.S. offer must be on terms at least as favorable as any other offer to the same class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. holders may be included in the foreign offer(s) only where home jurisdiction law precludes exclusion and offer materials to U.S. holders fully and adequately disclose risks of participating in the foreign offer(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier II exemption — notice of extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of extensions made according to home jurisdiction law/practice will satisfy § 240.14e-1(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Home jurisdiction procedures for announcing extensions are recognized for U.S. compliance in Tier II cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier II exemption — prompt payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment made in accordance with home jurisdiction law/practice will satisfy § 240.14e-1(c). If payment may not be made more quickly under home jurisdiction law, payment for securities tendered during any subsequent offering period within 20 business days of tender will satisfy prompt payment requirements of § 240.14d-11(e). Business day is determined with reference to the target's home jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines timing flexibility tied to home jurisdiction norms and specifies 20 business day rule for subsequent offering periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier II exemption — subsequent offering period/withdrawal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: A bidder will satisfy announcement and prompt payment requirements of § 240.14d-11(d) if the bidder announces results (including approximate number deposited) and pays in accordance with home jurisdiction law/practice and the subsequent offering period commences immediately following such announcement; bidder need not extend withdrawal rights following the close and prior to commencement of subsequent offering period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns U.S. subsequent offering period mechanics with home jurisdiction practice where conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier II exemption — payment of interest on subsequent tenders
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding § 240.14d-11(f), bidder may pay interest on securities tendered during a subsequent offering period if required under applicable foreign law; paying such interest will not be deemed to violate § 240.14d-10(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits compliance with foreign law requirements re interest without violating certain U.S. rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier II exemption — suspension of withdrawal rights during counting
rubrics_metrics.description: Bidder may suspend withdrawal rights at the end of the offer while tendered securities are being counted provided: (A) offer period including withdrawal rights was at least 20 U.S. business days; (B) when withdrawal rights are suspended, all offer conditions have been satisfied or waived except when counting to determine minimum acceptance; (C) suspension is only during counting and withdrawal rights are reinstated immediately thereafter except to extent terminated by acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows temporary suspension of withdrawal rights during narrow counting window, subject to procedural safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier II exemption — mix-and-match elections and proration
rubrics_metrics.description: Where bidder offers choices between different forms of consideration, it may establish a ceiling on one or more forms, offset elections of tendering security holders against one another subject to proration, and separately offset/prorate securities tendered during initial and subsequent offering periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overrides certain § 240.14d-11(b)/(f) requirements to permit customary allocation/proration mechanics under home jurisdiction practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier II exemption — early termination of an initial offering period
rubrics_metrics.description: A bidder may terminate an initial offering period (including a voluntary extension) early if: (A) initial offering period has been open at least 20 U.S. business days; (B) bidder adequately discussed possibility/impact of early termination in original offer materials; (C) bidder provides a subsequent offering period after termination; (D) all offer conditions are satisfied when initial offering ends; (E) bidder does not terminate during any mandatory extension required under U.S. tender offer rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits early termination only with prior disclosure and protections including subsequent offering period and satisfaction of conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home jurisdiction definition (Instruction 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Home jurisdiction means both the jurisdiction of the subject company's incorporation, organization or chartering and the principal foreign market where the subject company's securities are listed or quoted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used throughout to determine applicable foreign laws/practices for Tier I/II relief and timing/business day determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. holder definition and calculation method (Instruction 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. holder means any security holder resident in the United States. To determine percentage held by U.S. holders (absent Instruction 3 exceptions): (i) calculate U.S. ownership as of a date no more than 60 days before and no more than 30 days after public announcement (or most recent practicable date not earlier than 120 days before); (ii) include securities underlying American Depositary Shares convertible/exchangeable into subject securities; exclude other convertible/exchangeable securities (warrants/options) and securities held by bidder; (iii) use Rule 12g3-2(a) method for record ownership with limited inquiry to nominees in specified jurisdictions; (iv) if unable to obtain nominee account info after reasonable inquiry, assume customers are residents of nominee's principal place of business; (v) count securities as beneficially owned by U.S. residents as reported on beneficial ownership reports provided or filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes precise timing windows and inclusion/exclusion rules for calculating U.S. ownership percentage, and permissible assumptions where information cannot be obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptions for offers by non-affiliate bidders (Instruction 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a tender offer by a bidder other than an affiliate not made pursuant to an agreement with the issuer, the issuer will be presumed a foreign private issuer and U.S. holders presumed to hold <10% (<40% for paragraph (d)) unless Instruction 3.i-iii indicate otherwise. If bidder is unable to conduct U.S. ownership analysis, bidder may presume <10% (<40% for paragraph (d)) so long as there is a primary trading market outside U.S., unless certain volume/filing/knowledge exceptions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions that rebut presumptions include average daily U.S. trading volume thresholds, issuer filings indicating >10% (or >40%) U.S. ownership, or bidder knowledge/reason to know U.S. ownership exceeds thresholds. Provides example sources of bidder knowledge (public filings, issuer information, advisors, third-party providers).

rubrics_metrics.name: United States definition (Instruction 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: United States means the United States of America, its territories and possessions, any State of the United States, and the District of Columbia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies geographic scope for residency, business day, and other references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-evasion rule for exemptions (Instruction 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemptions in paragraphs (c) and (d) are not available for any securities transaction or series of transactions that technically complies with those paragraphs but are part of a plan or scheme to evade Regulations 14D or 14E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves substantive integrity of exemptions and authorizes denial where scheme to evade exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press-related materials exception (paragraph (e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision that requirements of sections 14(d)(1)-(7), Regulation 14D, and certain Regulation 14E sections shall not apply merely because a bidder for securities of a foreign private issuer provides journalists with access to press conferences, meetings, or written press-related materials held/released outside the U.S., provided: (1) access is provided to both U.S. and foreign journalists; (2) written press materials discussing a present/proposed tender offer for Section 12-registered equity securities must state the materials are not an extension of a U.S. tender offer; if bidder intends to extend the offer to the U.S. later it must state that and that Williams Act requirements will be satisfied then; no means to tender securities or coupons may be provided or attached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows limited press outreach outside U.S. without triggering U.S. tender offer rules so long as communications are balanced, disclaimers included, and no tender mechanisms provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption that target qualifies as a foreign private issuer for § 240.14d-1(e) (paragraph (f))
rubrics_metrics.description: A bidder may presume that a target qualifies as a foreign private issuer if the target is a foreign issuer and files registration statements/reports designated for foreign private issuers, claims exemption under § 240.12g3-2(b), or is not reporting in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a practical basis for relying on press-materials exception when target has affirmatively identified itself or filed as a foreign private issuer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — beneficial owner (paragraph (g)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The term beneficial owner has the same meaning as in Rule 13d-3, except that (except for Rule 14d-3 and Rule 14d-9(d)) it does not include a person who does not have or share investment power or who is deemed a beneficial owner by virtue of Rule 13d-3(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references Rule 13d-3 and notes limited exceptions for other specified rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — bidder (paragraph (g)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The term bidder means any person who makes a tender offer or on whose behalf a tender offer is made; provided, however, that the term does not include an issuer which makes a tender offer for securities of any class of which it is the issuer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies who is considered a bidder for application of the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — business day (paragraph (g)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Business day means any day other than Saturday, Sunday or a federal holiday, and consists of the period from 12:01 a.m. through 12:00 midnight Eastern time; when computing time periods under sections 14(d)(5) or 14(d)(6) or under Regulations 14D/14E, include date of event unless event occurs on a non-business day, in which case period begins on and includes first business day thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes time computation rules tied to Eastern time and federal holidays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — initial offering period (paragraph (g)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial offering period means the period from time the offer commences until all minimum time periods, including extensions required by Regulations 14D/14E have been satisfied and all conditions to the offer have been satisfied or waived within these time periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in timing and withdrawal-rights rules across the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — security holders (paragraph (g)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Security holders means holders of record and beneficial owners of securities which are the subject of a tender offer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad definition to include both record and beneficial holders for distribution and treatment requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — security position listing (paragraph (g)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Security position listing means, with respect to securities of any issuer held by a registered clearing agency in the name of the clearing agency or its nominee, a list of those participants in the clearing agency on whose behalf the clearing agency holds the issuer's securities and of the participants' respective positions in such securities as of a specified date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for establishing positions and calculating outstanding securities when clearing agency holds central positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — subject company (paragraph (g)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject company means any issuer of securities which are sought by a bidder pursuant to a tender offer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminology used throughout the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — subsequent offering period (paragraph (g)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsequent offering period means the period immediately following the initial offering period meeting the conditions specified in § 240.14d-11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triggers special proration/withdrawal and payment rules when a subsequent offering period commences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — tender offer material (paragraph (g)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: Tender offer material means: (i) the bidder's formal offer, including all material terms/conditions and amendments; (ii) the related transmittal letter and amendments; (iii) press releases, advertisements, letters and other documents published or sent by the bidder to security holders which directly or indirectly solicit, invite or request tenders of the securities being sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad definition that includes many forms of communications; used to determine what communications are considered part of the tender offer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatures requirement for filings (paragraph (h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents filed with or furnished to the Commission that require a signature must be manually signed, or signed using typed, duplicated, or facsimile versions of manual signatures. Where such signatures are used, each signatory must manually or electronically sign an authentication document executed before or at time of filing and retained by the filer for five years; requirements of § 232.302(b) apply to electronic authentication documents. Upon request, filer must furnish copies of retained documents to the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies acceptable signature forms, retention period for authentication documents (5 years), and availability to Commission upon request.
